consumer.use: Decide whether the passed R3 v3 Outcome-Bound admission semantics are feasible on the first three prospective natural Bureau operator-intake identity births without delaying productive work.

decision_target.question: Can exactly three first-in-order post-activation candidate_identity_birth slots be prospectively admitted under C/S/B/E/T/Q with zero binding failures, zero authority violations, zero backfill and median handling <= 10 minutes?

intervention.name: R3-v3 prospective three-slot admission
intervention.description: The experiment is registered as active testing before A while execution_status remains designed. After reviewed merge, set A to one explicit Bureau activation-marker event id; then consume the first three fully provable later candidate identity births in numeric event-id order and attempt C/S/B/E/T/Q binding before productive mutation without delaying work.

control_condition.description: The last three fully provable canonical candidate identity births with event_id < A are frozen after A only as negative eligibility sentinels: each must remain excluded because it predates A. They are not pilot cases and their outcomes are not compared for efficacy.

treatment_condition.description: Exactly the first three fully provable canonical candidate identity births with identity_first_event.event_id > A, subject to the inherited R3 v3 hard birth-proof and self-interference rules.

measurement.method: Before A, bind this experiment in experiments/active.v1.json as state testing with results/decision.yml verdict not_executed and manifest execution_status designed. After exact-head review and merge, create one idempotent Bureau marker whose numeric event id becomes A. For each consumed post-A slot, the terminal-state mapping is fixed: frozen and not_applicable add 0; capture_missed_before_mutation, capture_not_frozen_in_time, result_informed_binding_failure, indeterminate, rejected_interference and rejected_ambiguous_causation each add 1 and immediately REJECT. Each slot gets deterministic slot_id from experiment id, A, ordinal, canonical candidate id and birth event id. Before A, freeze a terminal_journal_contract for one already-existing durable controller evidence journal; if no existing surface proves caller-keyed idempotent append, exact authoritative readback/absence, fenced/linearizable absence after an ambiguous append that proves the earlier append cannot later become visible, restart durability, and an immutable provider-returned lowercase SHA-256 record_sha256, A MUST NOT be written. Before terminal evidence mutation, append and read-back-verify a complete write-ahead slot_terminal_intent through that frozen journal contract; terminal and failure records bind the provider-returned intent record_sha256, never a client-computed structured-object hash. A verified intent with neither matching terminal nor failure receipt mechanically derives persistence_outcome_unknown across controller restarts and blocks every later ordinal until reconciliation. Terminal/failure writes are idempotent and ambiguous outcomes are read-only reconciled before retry. A failure record may be created after an ambiguous terminal append only behind that fenced absence. If both terminal and failure records ever coexist, the failure record deterministically dominates and the pilot immediately REJECTS with dual_terminal_failure_records.
measurement.success: 3/3 canonical slots, binding_failure_count == 0, zero material review disagreements, zero authority violations, zero replacement/backfill, median handling_seconds <= 600, at least two definitive non-D0 cases, and no durable unresolved terminal intent.
measurement.falsification: Any state with binding_failure_increment=1, experiment interference, ambiguous causation, authority violation, replacement/backfill, noncanonical ordering, post-result binding, material exact-head review disagreement, dual terminal/failure records, or durable unresolved terminal intent at closeout rejects the revision.

cost_metric.method: For every consumed slot, sample handling_started_at_monotonic_ns immediately before the first authoritative candidate-task read in the scan that discovers the candidate or begins its eligibility proof. After detection, completeness scans, identity/birth proof, evidence reads, analysis and failed-capture classification have produced a complete provisional terminal payload in memory, sample handling_finished_at_monotonic_ns immediately before persistence. handling_seconds is their monotonic difference divided by 1e9. Through the frozen terminal_journal_contract, append/read-back-verify a complete deterministic write-ahead terminal intent and retain its provider-returned record_sha256 before any terminal evidence mutation; terminal persistence latency is excluded from handling_seconds. A replacement controller derives persistence_outcome_unknown whenever a verified intent lacks both matching terminal and failure receipts, and must reconcile that earlier ordinal before handling any later birth. An ambiguous terminal append may authorize a failure record only after fenced/linearizable absence proves the terminal cannot later appear; any dual terminal/failure state deterministically REJECTS. PASS requires the three-slot median <= 600 seconds and no durable unresolved intent.

comparison.unit: three fixed pre-A negative eligibility sentinels versus three post-A pilot slots
comparability_constraints: activation boundary is the Bureau marker event id A, not a retrospectively selected timestamp
only identity_first_event.event_id ascending determines slot order
no replacement or backfill after any slot outcome
R3 v3 sampling semantics remain unchanged
no Full Outcome Case is collected
confounders: the first three births may contain too few informative non-D0 cases
observer independence may be hard to prove for some slots
three cases establish only tiny-sample feasibility, not product efficacy

fresh Bureau live-list completeness signals with coverage_complete=true and projection_source=complete_event_scan

monotonic handling-clock boundaries plus UTC provenance timestamps
